title: Finite initial truncation of the opposite simplicial indexing category
statement: Let $S$ be a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] such that every $S_n$ is finite and nonempty and $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Define a category $\mathcal I_S$ whose objects are pairs $(n,s)$ with $s\in S_n$, and whose morphisms $(m,t)\to(n,s)$ are order-preserving maps $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ satisfying $S(\varphi)(s)=t$. Choose $m_0\geq0$ such that every simplex in degree $n>m_0$ is degenerate, and let $\mathcal I_{S,\leq r}$ be the full subcategory on objects $(n,s)$ with $n\leq r$. Then the finite full subcategory $\mathcal I_{S,\leq 2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is initial in $\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ in these explicit senses: (1) for every object $z$ of $\mathcal I_S$ there is an object $y$ of $\mathcal I_{S,\leq 2m_0}$ and a morphism $z\to y$ in $\mathcal I_S$; (2) for any two morphisms $z\to y$ and $z\to y'$ with $y,y'$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq 2m_0}$, there are objects $y=y_0,y_1,\ldots,y_{2r}=y'$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq 2m_0}$ and a zigzag $y_0\to y_1\leftarrow y_2\to\cdots\leftarrow y_{2r}$ in $\mathcal I_S$, together with morphisms $z\to y_i$ extending the two given ones, such that composing $z\to y_i$ with each adjacent arrow gives $z\to y_{i+1}$ (or conversely for an arrow pointing left). Consequently, for every category $\mathcal C$ and diagram $D:\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$, Categories Lemma 002R identifies the limit of $D$ over $\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the limit of its restriction to the finite category $\mathcal I_{S,\leq 2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}$, whenever either limit exists.

proof.text: Setup and finiteness. $\mathcal I_S$ is a category: the identity of $[n]$ is a morphism $(n,s)\to(n,s)$, and if $\varphi:(m,t)\to(n,s)$ and $\varphi':(n,s)\to(p,r)$ then $S(\varphi'\circ\varphi)(r)=S(\varphi)(S(\varphi')(r))=S(\varphi)(s)=t$ by functoriality of $S$, so $\varphi'\circ\varphi:(m,t)\to(p,r)$. An integer $m_0$ as in the statement exists because $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices (take the largest degree of a nondegenerate simplex, or $0$). The full subcategory $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}$ is finite: its objects form the finite set $\coprod_{n\leq2m_0}S_n$ (each $S_n$ is finite), and the morphisms $(m,t)\to(n,s)$ form a subset of the finite set of order-preserving maps $[m]\to[n]$.

proof.text: Every object maps to one of degree at most $m_0$; this proves (1). Let $z=(n,s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] there are $r\geq0$, a surjective order-preserving $\sigma:[n]\to[r]$ and a nondegenerate $u\in S_r$ with $s=S(\sigma)(u)$. Since $u$ is nondegenerate, $r\leq m_0$ by the choice of $m_0$. Thus $\sigma$ is a morphism $z\to(r,u)$ in $\mathcal I_S$ with $(r,u)$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq m_0}\subseteq\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}$, which is (1).

proof.text: Combinatorial claim. Let $k>2m_0$ and let $\varphi:[k]\to[n]$, $\varphi':[k]\to[n']$ be order-preserving with $n,n'\leq m_0$. Then there is $0\leq i\leq2m_0$ (so $i\leq k-1$) with $\varphi(i)=\varphi(i+1)$ and $\varphi'(i)=\varphi'(i+1)$. Indeed, call $i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ an ascent of $\varphi$ if $\varphi(i)<\varphi(i+1)$; as $\varphi$ is order-preserving, $\varphi(k)-\varphi(0)$ is at least the number of ascents, so $\varphi$ has at most $n\leq m_0$ ascents, and likewise $\varphi'$ has at most $m_0$. Among the $2m_0+1$ indices $0,1,\ldots,2m_0$ at most $2m_0$ are ascents of $\varphi$ or of $\varphi'$, so one index $i$ is an ascent of neither, i.e. $\varphi(i)=\varphi(i+1)$ and $\varphi'(i)=\varphi'(i+1)$.

proof.text: Descent to degree at most $2m_0$. Claim: for every object $z=(k,w)$ and morphisms $\varphi:z\to(n,u)$, $\varphi':z\to(n',u')$ of $\mathcal I_S$ with $n,n'\leq m_0$, there are an object $a=(k',v)$ with $k'\leq2m_0$ and morphisms $\tau:z\to a$, $\psi:a\to(n,u)$, $\psi':a\to(n',u')$ with $\psi\circ\tau=\varphi$ and $\psi'\circ\tau=\varphi'$. Induction on $k$. If $k\leq2m_0$ take $a=z$, $\tau=\mathrm{id}$, $\psi=\varphi$, $\psi'=\varphi'$. If $k>2m_0$, step 3 gives $i\leq k-1$ with $\varphi(i)=\varphi(i+1)$, $\varphi'(i)=\varphi'(i+1)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-degeneracy-factorization] gives order-preserving $\psi_1:[k-1]\to[n]$, $\psi_1':[k-1]\to[n']$ with $\varphi=\psi_1\circ\sigma^{k-1}_i$, $\varphi'=\psi_1'\circ\sigma^{k-1}_i$. Put $v_1=S(\psi_1)(u)$, $v_1'=S(\psi_1')(u')$. Then $s^{k-1}_i(v_1)=S(\sigma^{k-1}_i)(S(\psi_1)(u))=S(\varphi)(u)=w=S(\varphi')(u')=s^{k-1}_i(v_1')$, and $s^{k-1}_i:S_{k-1}\to S_k$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-degeneracy-injective], so $v_1=v_1'$. Hence $z_1=(k-1,v_1)$ is an object with morphisms $\sigma^{k-1}_i:z\to z_1$ (as $S(\sigma^{k-1}_i)(v_1)=w$), $\psi_1:z_1\to(n,u)$ and $\psi_1':z_1\to(n',u')$. The induction hypothesis for $z_1$ and $\psi_1,\psi_1'$ gives $a$ with $k'\leq2m_0$, $\tau_1:z_1\to a$, $\psi,\psi'$ with $\psi\circ\tau_1=\psi_1$, $\psi'\circ\tau_1=\psi_1'$; then $\tau=\tau_1\circ\sigma^{k-1}_i$ satisfies $\psi\circ\tau=\psi_1\circ\sigma^{k-1}_i=\varphi$ and $\psi'\circ\tau=\varphi'$.

Since $s^{k-1}_i$ is injective, see Lemma 016F, we conclude that $U(\psi)(u)=U(\psi')(u')$ also. Continuing in this fashion ... with $a\in\mathcal U_{\leq2m_0}$'

proof.text: The zigzag; this proves (2). Let $\alpha:z\to y$ and $\alpha':z\to y'$ be morphisms with $y,y'$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}$. By step 2 there are morphisms $\beta:y\to u$, $\beta':y'\to u'$ with $u,u'$ of degree at most $m_0$. Step 4 applied to $\beta\circ\alpha:z\to u$ and $\beta'\circ\alpha':z\to u'$ gives $a$ of degree at most $2m_0$ and $\tau:z\to a$, $\psi:a\to u$, $\psi':a\to u'$ with $\psi\circ\tau=\beta\circ\alpha$, $\psi'\circ\tau=\beta'\circ\alpha'$. Take $r=2$ and $y_0=y\xrightarrow{\beta}y_1=u\xleftarrow{\psi}y_2=a\xrightarrow{\psi'}y_3=u'\xleftarrow{\beta'}y_4=y'$, all in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}$ (as $m_0\leq2m_0$), with $z\to y_i$ equal to $\alpha$, $\beta\circ\alpha$, $\tau$, $\beta'\circ\alpha'$, $\alpha'$. The compatibilities are $\beta\circ\alpha=(z\to y_1)$, $\psi\circ\tau=\beta\circ\alpha$, $\psi'\circ\tau=\beta'\circ\alpha'$ and $\beta'\circ\alpha'=(z\to y_3)$, which hold by construction.

proof.text: Limit comparison. Let $H:\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the inclusion. A morphism $H(x)\to z$ in $\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a morphism $z\to x$ in $\mathcal I_S$, and a sequence $x_0\leftarrow x_1\rightarrow x_2\leftarrow\cdots\rightarrow x_{2r}$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}$ with compatible $H(x_i)\to z$ is a zigzag $x_0\to x_1\leftarrow x_2\to\cdots\leftarrow x_{2r}$ in $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}$ with compatible $z\to x_i$; so (1) and (2), proved in steps 2 and 5, are hypotheses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] for $H$. That node, applied to $M=D:\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$, gives: $D$ has a limit if and only if $D\circ H$ (the restriction to the finite category $\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}$) has one, every cone on the restriction extends to a cone on $D$ with the same vertex, a cone on $D$ is a limit iff its restriction is, and the canonical morphism $\varprojlim_{\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}}D\to\varprojlim_{\mathcal I_{S,\leq2m_0}^{\mathrm{op}}}D|$ is an isomorphism.
